title: Skate or Die!
build: PAL, two-sided G64 pair supplied by the contributor (side 1 SHA-256 45e07b32..., side 2 7a402586...); EA loader, no crack or trainer

records.c: 6510 data-direction register. The Freestyle program never writes it; its only reference is the indexed zero-page clear at $1671 (STA $00,X), which starts at X = $12, so $00 itself is never touched.

6510 port: memory configuration. The ramp sets $25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000-$DFFF, no ROMs) at $0886, $08A1 and $0A17, so the music at $E000 and the resident code at $F230 are visible.

Load stub, copied here by the resident event manager ($FA58 copies 29 bytes from its template at $F925 and patches the file number and addresses). This copy loads file $0D, the Freestyle ramp program ($31FF bytes per the loader table at $F2F9, so $0880-$3A7E), through JSR $F230 with X/Y = $0880, sets CIA 1 port A as outputs and port B as inputs, drives $7F on port A (keyboard row 7 only) and jumps to $0880. $081C is the template's 29th byte ($AD); $081D-$087F are zero and unused.

Event entry, the stub's jump target. As loaded these three bytes are JMP $0886 (first-time set-up; file $0D starts 4C 86 08); $0896-$08A0 overwrite them with NOPs, so any later jump here (PRACTICE AGAIN re-runs the stub's JMP $0880 without loading) falls through to JMP $08A1, the per-entry initialisation.
Second byte of the entry JMP $0886 ($86 as loaded), replaced by NOP ($EA) at $089B after the first entry.
Third byte of the entry JMP $0886 ($08 as loaded), replaced by NOP ($EA) at $089E; execution then runs on into JMP $08A1 at $0883.

First-time set-up, run once per load: $01 = $25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000), load the font file $0F to $6800 (load_glyph_file $15C5), load and unpack the half-pipe picture (load_ramp_picture), load the pose and shape files $11 and $12 (load_skater_data) and the music file $13 (load_music_file), then NOP out the JMP at $0880 and fall into ramp_init.

Per-entry initialisation: SEI, $01 = $25, wait for the frame wrap, black border and background, $D011 = $2B (bitmap mode, display blanked), clear zero page $12-$7F (clear_zero_page_vars), build the quarter-square table at $0400-$07FF and the bit-reverse tables at $3363/$3463, set up the bitmap video and colour RAM (init_bitmap_video), the status line and sprites (init_status_and_sprites), the raster interrupt (install_raster_irq), the sound driver ($271E) and the event state (init_event: music, score and passes to zero, a colour set, phase 0), then CLI into the main loop.

Main loop, outside the interrupt; never returns (the event leaves through JMP $FE06 at $1FB0, from inside the interrupt). If $7C is set (the Commodore key turned sound off, $1F74) re-run the sound initialiser $271E and clear $7C. If the sound-request ring's read index $7E differs from its write index $7D, take the next request ($1FC2) and pass it to the sound queue ($275C). If the tick count $7F (raised once a frame by the band-0 interrupt at $0B39) is nonzero, run one step of the sound driver ($2793) and decrement it.

Load file $10 (the same run-length packed half-pipe picture High Jump uses) to $4000 and keep the end address the loader returns in $16/$17; unpack $4000..end into $6E00 (unpack_rle $1FD1); then copy the unpacked picture out with copy_block: $1F40 bitmap bytes to $4000, $3E8 screen-matrix bytes to $6400 and $3E8 colour bytes to $6000, which init_bitmap_video copies into colour RAM on every entry. The $6E00 scratch area is then overwritten by file $11.

Load file $11 to $6E00 and keep the end address the loader returns in $3351/$3352, then load file $12 straight after it (X/Y still hold that end). The loader table at $F2F9 gives lengths $1284 and $402C, so the files fill $6E00-$8083 (158 pose records of 30 bytes) and $8084-$C0AF (the sprite shapes). These are the same two files High Jump loads, $200 lower in memory. $3351/$3352 is the base read_sprite_descriptor adds to each shape offset.

Inside load_skater_data (STY $3352). The automatic symbol comes from the RESET vector in RAM at $FFFC, which holds $0954 (written with the NMI vector by the page-3 code at $03AB, from an earlier program); the CPU never takes it here, since a hardware reset maps the KERNAL ROM in.
Load file $13 (the Freestyle music: phrase table, music scripts, machine code and note streams, $08C9 bytes) to $E000-$E8C8 and return through the loader (JMP $F230).

Point $2A/$2B at pose record A: $6E00 + A*30, using the quarter-square multiply multiply_8x8 ($16D3). Each record holds five 6-byte sprite parts; byte 3 of a part is its X offset and byte 4 its Y offset (place_part_sprite). Called from place_sprites and build_skater_graphics.
Add A to the 16-bit pointer $12/$13. Never called: no instruction and no byte pair in the 64 KB image names $0976. The same routine sits unused in High Jump at $096D.

Status line and sprite set-up: CIA 1 port A outputs ($7F, keyboard row 7) and port B inputs; colour the 40 cells of the hires status line from $3323 into screen row 0 at $6400 and write 6 into colour RAM row 0; print the inline text 'PASSES:' and 'SCORE:' (the 40 bytes after the JSR $15CE at $09A6, typed as data) into bitmap row 0, which returns to $09D2.

Inline argument of the JSR $15CE at $09A6, not code: the status-line text, ASCII masked to screen codes by $15E4, zero-terminated at $09D1: sixteen spaces, 'PASSES:', four spaces, 'SCORE:', seven spaces (40 cells). The name field on the left is printed over the leading spaces by $09D2.

Where $15CE returns after the inline text: print the skater's name from the pointer at $FE00/$FE01 (event manager slot A; 'PRACTICE' in practice) at cell 0, set the sprite buffer pointer $22 = $A8, sprite multicolours $D025 = 1 (white) and $D026 = 6 (blue), copy the skater attribute $FE02 into entry 4 (the board) of both sprite colour sets $3313 and $331B, build the first skater frame from pose $81 (push_off_poses[0]) and copy the two 64-byte score sprites from $31D5/$3215 to blocks $AD/$AE ($6B40/$6B80), shown as sprites 5 and 6.

Install the raster interrupt: SEI, $01 = $25, CIA 1 interrupts off ($DC0D = $7F, then read to acknowledge), wait for the frame wrap, band $1E = 0, clear the raster compare's bit 8, first compare line from $2E6C ($FB), IRQ vector $FFFE/$FFFF = $0AF4, enable the raster interrupt.

The NMI vector $FFFA holds $0A3A, which here is the operand byte $F4 of LDA #$F4 at $0A39. Nothing in this load writes $FFFA (High Jump's vector holds the same $0A3A, left by an earlier load). An NMI (the RESTORE key, with the KERNAL banked out) would decode F4 8D (NOP zp,x), FE FF A9 (INC $A9FF,X), ASL, STA $FFFF, LDA #$01, STA $D01A, RTS: it corrupts the IRQ vector's high byte and returns through the interrupt's stack frame with RTS. Not tested.

Wait until the raster line's low byte ($D012) falls, which happens when a new frame starts (PAL line $137 to 0); the 255-to-256 step reads as $FF to $00, which BMI sees as a rise, so it does not end the wait.

Bitmap video set-up: black border and background, copy $3E8 colour bytes from $6000 into colour RAM $D800 (copy_block), $D018 = $90 (screen matrix at $2400 and bitmap at $0000 within the bank), $DD00 bits 0-1 = %10 (VIC bank 1: screen $6400, bitmap $4000), $D016 = $18 (multicolour, 40 columns), $D011 = $3B (bitmap mode, display on, 25 rows, Y scroll 3). Returns with carry clear.

Copy Y*256+X bytes from the read pointer $12/$13 to the write pointer $14/$15, advancing both (read_ptr12_byte, write_ptr14_byte); $18/$19 count down the low and high parts. Used by load_ramp_picture and init_bitmap_video.

Never called: like copy_block but takes each byte from JSR $FFCF (CHRIN in the KERNAL jump table), which with $01 = $25 would run RAM. No instruction or byte pair in the image names $0AA6. Library code shared with High Jump ($0AA2 there).
Never called (no reference in the image): write Y*256+X zero bytes through the write pointer $14/$15.
Return the byte at ($12) in A and advance the pointer $12/$13; leaves Y = 0. Byte source for copy_block, unpack_rle and the inline-text printer.
Store A at ($14) and advance the pointer $14/$15; leaves Y = 0. Byte sink for copy_block, fill_block_zero, copy_block_from_ffcf and unpack_rle.
Never called (no reference in the image): JSR $FFE7 (CLALL), then repeat JSR $FFE4 (GETIN) until a key; with the KERNAL banked out those addresses hold RAM.

Raster interrupt entry (vector $FFFE): save A, X, Y, acknowledge $D019, take the handler for band $1E from the word table $2E68 ($0B25 for band 0, $0CCE for band 1) into the JSR at $0B0F, run it, then step to the next band ($2E6E) and set its compare line ($2E6C: $FB, then $38).
Operand of the JSR at $0B0F, rewritten every interrupt from $2E68/$2E69 with the current band's handler.
High byte of the JSR operand at $0B0F, rewritten every interrupt from $2E69 (the band handler's high byte). The code after it (from $0B12) steps to the next band and sets its raster line.

Band 0 handler, raster line $FB (below the picture): clear $D016's multicolour bit so the status line at the top of the next frame shows hires; position and colour the sprites (place_sprites); count the frame ($1950); poll RUN/STOP ($1F58) and the Commodore key ($1F74); add a sound tick to $7F. Then the trick-score pop-up: while the timer $2E runs it is counted down; on its first frame ($2F still 0) the pending trick score $2C/$2D is added to the total ($1D4E, which redraws SCORE), sound $14 is requested, the trick score's four digits are drawn into the sprites 5 and 6 ($18E3), the crowd timers are loaded ($53 = $30 + 2 * the trick score's hundreds byte, $52 = half of that), $2C/$2D are cleared and $2F = $60 turns sprites 5 and 6 on; when $2E reaches 0, $2F = 0 turns them off. Every fourth frame $53 counts down, then $52. Unless points were awarded this frame ($19), one flag animation at a 1-in-8 chance ($1ED5), otherwise two tries at a crowd cell ($1EE8).

Set the sprites for the frame: enable sprites 0-4, plus 5 and 6 while $2F = $60 (the trick-score pop-up) and 7 when $73 says so; no priority, X or Y expansion; multicolour for sprites 1 and 2 only ($D01C = 6). Pointers at $67F8: sprites 0-4 take $22..$22+4 (the skater buffer being shown), sprite 7 takes $22+4 as well (the board's shape, drawn in black), sprites 5 and 6 take $AD and $AE (the score digits at $6B40/$6B80). Positions: during a fall ($25 bit 7) sprites 0-3 come from the thrown body's pose $6C at $67/$68/$69 with its side $66, and sprite 4 (the board) from the fifth part of pose $5D at $58/$59/$5A; otherwise all five parts of pose $5D (place_part_sprite). Sprites 5 and 6 go to fixed places ($0CB2). Sprite 7 takes sprite 4's X and sprite 4's Y + $76 - $5A + 1 (the board's shadow on the ramp surface, $1517). $D010 is built from the bits gathered in $1B.

Position sprite $18 (register offset $19 = 2*$18) from the pose part at ($2A): Y = $79 + part byte 4; X = $77/$78 + part byte 3 when the side byte $1A has bit 7 set (right half of the ramp), or $77/$78 minus byte 3 otherwise ($0C93), which mirrors the figure about its origin; the X high bit is rotated into $1B for $D010.

Position score sprite 5 (Y = 0) or 6 (Y = 1) at a fixed place: X = $A0 + $3255[Y] (160 or 184), Y = $A0 + $3257[Y] (160 for both), X high bit 0 rotated into $1B. The two sprites sit side by side in the middle of the ramp.

Band 1 handler, raster line $38: busy-wait for line $3A, then set $D016's multicolour bit for the picture. Then the frame's game update: read the controls and run the current phase (read_controls_and_run_phase); clamp the depth $5F/$60 to $A8-$108 (clamp_depth $1D70); if the side bit $57 differs from last frame's $20 (the skater crossed the middle of the ramp), set $42 = $FF (trick class to be chosen again), clear the pump-done flag $26 and set $27 = 1, and rebuild the skater graphics; otherwise rebuild them only when the pose $5D (or, in a fall, the thrown body's pose $6C) changed. Save $5D, $57, $6C in $1F, $20, $21, copy the animation step $38 to $4A, update sprite 7 ($1F3A), then run animate_crowd_cell until raster line $DC or ten times.

Read the controls: $DC01 (joystick port 1) AND $DC00 (joystick port 2) into $35, active low: bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire. Port A drives $7F, so keyboard row 7 also reaches $DC01: SPACE reads as fire, 1 as up, the left-arrow key as down, CTRL as left and 2 as right. $36 = new OR NOT old, so a bit of $36 is 0 only on the frame its line goes from released to pressed. Then jump to the handler for phase $34 through the word table $2F81, patched into the JMP at $0D55.
Operand of the JMP at $0D55, rewritten each frame from the phase table $2F81/$2F82 by read_controls_and_run_phase.
High byte of the JMP operand at $0D55, rewritten each frame from $2F82.

Phase 0, standing on the left platform: clear the fall flag $25 and the crowd timers $52/$53, set the path position $62/$63 = $0056 (the platform) and look it up ($162C). While the push-off counters $37/$38 are zero: let the stick move the skater across the ramp ($1C14), and if fire was not just pressed, start the fidget animation (phase $1A, variant $39 = random 0 or 1) when random_below($55) returns 0 (a random byte of 0-3: 4 in 256 per frame). Fire starts the push-off: $37 counts six frames per step of $38, ten steps (60 frames) with pose $5D = push_off_poses[$38]; at the end phase 2 begins at the top of the wall ($146A), the trick class $42 = 2 and the fakie flag $24 = 0, and phase 2 runs at once (JMP $0D35).

Phase $1A, the fidget animation on the platform: stick across the ramp ($1C14), keep the platform position ($162C) and display coordinates ($14AF). If fire has just been pressed, clear the counters and run phase 0 at once, which starts the push-off. Otherwise $37 counts six frames per step of $38; the pose $5D is fidget_poses_a[$38] for variant $39 = 0 or fidget_poses_b[$38] for variant 1; when $38 reaches fidget_lengths[$39] (12 for both) the counters clear and phase 0 resumes.

Phase 2, riding the ramp: stick up and down moves across the ramp ($1C01); move along the path ($1487), friction ($1B7C), the swoosh sounds ($1BC2). Above the coping height ($23 < $96) the skater leaves the ramp at $0E69. Otherwise the zone is the first triple of ride_pose_zones ($2E95) whose threshold exceeds $23 ($18 = 0, 3, 6, 9 or 12 for y below $BA, $D6, $E3, $EC, $FF); the pose is the triple's second byte, or its third when the fakie flag $24 is set. Holding fire uses ride_pose_zones_fire ($2EA4) instead, a crouch in the lowest zone, and calls pump_check ($1BAF). A pose of $FF (the top zone) means the trick-class pose: if $42 is $FF (reset at every centre crossing) the class is chosen now (choose_trick_class $1C81); the lean flags $40/$41 are cleared on every frame in this zone, and the pose is class_ride_poses[$42] (class_ride_poses_fakie with $24). In the zones below the top one, lean_check ($1C56) records a left or right press.

Phase 2 reaching the coping: record the channel side in $49 (0 when on the right half; leaving the left wall it is $7F or $FF, bit 7 set when the depth is $E0 or more, $1E32), redraw PASSES ($1CD1), then start the phase for the trick class: class_phases[$42] (4 air for classes 0 and 1, 6, $12, $16, $18, or $1C for class 6, the end of the run).

Phase $0A, a fall: set $25 = $FF (sprites 0-3 then show the thrown body, object 1). If the depth is off the ramp's width ($1D26) the skater drops off the side (fall_off_side $1DCB); otherwise the depth slides ($1D97), the board keeps moving along the path with double friction and takes the zone pose from $2E96. The body then follows the fall type $28: type 2 ($0F15) slides along the path as object 1 and takes a pose from fall_slide_poses by its height $65; types 0 and 1 are first thrown ballistically ($184A, pose from fall_air_poses by $65) until $65 reaches $F0, then lie through fall_type_lengths[$28] (4 or 14) poses from fall_lie_poses_0/_1, eight frames each, moving $64 by fall_lie_drift[$28]. Once it is over, fire returns to the platform (phase 0), or after the tenth pass ($4C >= 10) sets the depth to $C8 and ends the run (phase $1E).

Phase 4, in the air above the coping: the stick spins (air_spin_controls $1B10: left or right) and drifts across the ramp (air_depth_controls $1B31: up or down); move along the path. While still above the coping ($23 < $96) fire held in pose 8, $0C, $10 or $14 starts a grab ($0FF2). Coming back down: off the ramp's width is a fall of type 1 ($0F9B); over the channel ($1D0A), still spinning ($39 bit 6) or a pose whose low three bits are not 0, 1 or 7 (not facing forwards or backwards) is a fall of type 2. The pose also sets the fakie flag $24 ($FF when the pose, folded into $08-$17, is $0C-$13). A clean landing scores ($0FA0).

Score a clean landing: the spin count $29 rounded to the nearest half turn, ($29 + 3) AND $F8 (8 steps of the 16-pose spin per half turn). Trick class 1: add class1_air_scores[half turns] (100, 200, 400, 800, 1600) to the trick score $2C/$2D and set bit 1 of the trick-variety bits $50. Other classes: add air_scores[half turns * 16 + $4B], $4B being the grab count, (25 to 775 with no turn, 100 to 1250 for a half turn, 250 to 1750, 550 to 2425, 1150 to 3400 for two turns) and set bit 0 of $50. Decimal-mode adds. Then back to phase 2. Neither index is limited: five half turns or more, or a grab count of 16 or more, reads past the table.

In the air with fire held (fire released returns at once): in pose 8 or $10 (forwards or backwards) add 1 to the grab count $4B and clear the depth drift $47; in pose $0C or $14 (side on) add 2 and keep $47. Point $1C/$1D at the grab's pose pair ($2EE7, $2EE9, $2EEB or $2EED for poses 8, $0C, $10, $14), save the pose in $3D and enter phase $0C. Any other pose does nothing.

Phase 6, trick class 2 (a lean in the direction of travel with fewer than two pumps), entered with 200 points ($1957): the skater stays at the coping. Once any pump was made ($3F), up and down drift across the ramp ($1B31, which also starts sound 23). Over the channel, off the ramp's width or back below the coping is a fall (type 2, 0, 2), and pokes $3719 = 1 to end sound 23. The pose steps through plant_poses (plant_poses_fakie with $24), three frames each, and holds the fifth; while held it adds 2 points a frame, 4 while drifting ($3A bit 6). Fire then lets go (phase 8); left or right turns out of it (phase $10, which doubles the trick score), $39 recording whether the press was towards the side of the ramp the skater is on.

Phase 8, letting go of the class-2 plant with fire: fall checks as in phase 6 (channel, width, below the coping); the plant poses run backwards, three frames each; after five steps set bit 2 of the variety bits $50 and go back to phase 2 at the top of the wall ($146A).

Phase $10, leaving the class-2 plant with a left or right press; entering it doubled the trick score and ended sound 23 ($1957). Fall checks as in phase 6; eight poses three frames each from plant_turn_poses (four tables, by the fakie flag $24 and the direction flag $39); then the trick class becomes 1, the fakie flag flips, bit 2 of $50 is set and phase 2 resumes at the top of the wall.

Phase $12, trick class 3 (a lean against the direction of travel after two pumps), entered with 500 points. Over the channel, off the width or back below the coping is a fall. The pose steps through hold_poses_a (hold_poses_b with $24), six frames each, and holds the third; with $24 set, reaching the third step moves the depth $12 back (depth - $12). While held it adds 5 points a frame, and fire, left or right goes to phase $14: fire flips the fakie flag $24, left sets it on the left half and clears it on the right, right does the opposite.

Phase $14, the end of class 3: fall checks as in phase $12; the three poses run backwards, six frames each (with $24 set, step 1 moves the depth $12 forward again); then set bit 3 of $50 and go back to phase 2 at the top of the wall.

Phase $16, trick class 4 (a lean against the direction of travel after one pump), entered with 300 points and $39 = $FF if left or right was held then. Each frame the depth drifts by +$55/256 ($AB, that is -$55/256, with $24); over the channel or off the width is a fall (there is no coping check here). Five poses, eight frames each, from turn_poses_a (turn_poses_b when $39 is set), in reverse order with $24; then the fakie flag flips, bit 4 of $50 is set and phase 2 resumes at the top of the wall.

Phase $0C, the start of a grab: up and down drift ($1B31); the depth drifts by $47 each frame ($1CF0); move. Back below the coping is a fall ($1435). The two poses of the pair at ($1C) follow. The step test compares A, which still holds $23 (always 4 or more here), instead of the frame counter $37, so the pose steps every frame rather than every fourth; after two steps, phase $0E.

Phase $0E, holding a grab: up and down drift; the depth drifts by $47; move; back below the coping is a fall ($1435). While the counters are still zero and fire is held, add 2 points a frame and keep holding. Once fire is released the pose pair runs backwards, four frames a step; then the pose saved in $3D comes back and phase 4 resumes.

Phase $18, trick class 5 (a lean against the direction of travel with no pump), entered with 250 points. Each frame the depth drifts by +$7F/256 ($81, -$7F/256, with $24). Over the channel is a fall of type 2; off the width calls the fall with type 0 and then again with type 2, so the second call wins. Nine poses two frames each from spin_poses (reversed with $24); then the fakie flag flips, bit 5 of $50 is set and phase 2 resumes at the top of the wall.
Phase $1C, trick class 6, given once the pass count $4C has reached 11: the skater does not take off; seven poses, six frames each, from end_poses (end_poses_fakie with $24), then phase $1E.

Phase $1E, the end of the run (entered with the variety bonus, $1E48): on the platform, sound 6 on the first frame, nine poses ten frames each chosen by the total score: final_poses_low under 2,500, final_poses_mid under 10,000 (from $44/$45), final_poses_high above. After the ninth, fire ends the event (end_event $1F99).

Fall for a skater who comes back below the coping in a grab (phases $0C and $0E): off the ramp's width, fall type 1 with the speed zeroed ($1457); otherwise fall type 1 if random_below(10) returns 1, else type 0, and the board keeps the start speed of the side ($1E3B) after being put back at the top of the wall ($146F).
Start a fall of type A ($28: 0, 1 or 2): phase $0A, put the skater back at the top of the wall of the side it is on ($146F) with the speed $5B/$5C zeroed.
Enter phase 2 (set_phase), then place the skater at the top of the wall of the side it is on.
Set the path position $62/$63 to the top of the wall the skater is on: $0056 on the left half ($57 bit 7 clear), $01CC (= $222 - $56) on the right.

Move the skater (object 0) one frame along the path (integrate_object_motion $17D7, then $162C), copy its y $56 to $23, and while not falling, if the trick class $42 asks for it (class_hold_coping[$42], classes 2-6), keep the displayed y from rising above the coping ($96). Then compute the display position ($14AF).
Move object 1 (X = $0F, the thrown body in a type-2 fall) along the path ($17D7, $162C) and compute its display position ($14B3).
Display position of object 0 (the skater): with X = 0, falls into display_position.

Display position of object X (0 the skater, $0F the thrown body): perspective by the depth $5F/$60+X about the centre x = $B7: display x = $B7 - ($B7 - x) * depth / 256, display y = ($56 - 7) * depth / 256 + 7 (multiply_8x8, the high byte $60 adding one more whole times). Then to sprite coordinates: on the left half x - $0B, on the right half $163 - x (16-bit, $58/$59+X), y - $0A ($5A+X).

Sprite 7's reference point ($74-$76): while the skater is above the coping ($56 < $96) its display x with the coping line's y at the current depth ($8F * depth / 256 + 7 - $0A, which is y = $96 put through display_position); otherwise the skater's own display position. place_sprites puts sprite 7 at sprite 4's Y + $76 - $5A + 1, so the board's black copy stays on the ramp surface below a jump. Reached from update_sprite7 ($1F47).

One frame of a spin in the left-press mode ($1B2A): on the right half it takes the subtracting branch ($157C) instead. Add the spin rate $3C plus one (SEC, ADC) to the fraction $28; on a carry count a step in $29 and step the pose back by one within its 16-pose ring ($08-$17 or $18-$27). Then drift the depth by $33/256 ($47 = $33, $1CF0).

One frame of a spin in the right-press mode ($1B2D): on the right half it takes the adding branch ($1552) instead. Subtract the rate $3C plus one (CLC, SBC) from $28; on a borrow count a step in $29 and step the pose forward within its ring. Drift the depth by -$33/256 ($47 = $CD).
Draw A's high nibble as a digit at cell Y (shift down, then the body of draw_digit at $15AB). Used for the score's even digits ($1CB7, $1CC5).

Draw A's low nibble as one glyph at status-line cell Y ($1620): from the digit glyph codes at $31C5 (0-9, A-F). A zero while $46 is zero draws a space ($20) instead (leading-zero blanking); a nonzero digit sets $46.
Load file $0F, the font, to $6800 (JMP $F230 with X/Y = $6800). Called once from the first-time set-up.

Print the zero-terminated string that follows the JSR into the status line at the cell set by A ($1620), then return past the string: pull the return address into $12/$13, step it past the address ($0AD5), print through print_glyph_string, push $12/$13 and RTS. Its one call is at $09A6, the text at $09A9-$09D1. Never disassemble a range that includes that call: the text decodes as instructions.
Print the zero-terminated string at ($12) to $14/$15: each byte masked with $3F (ASCII to screen code) and drawn by copy_inverted_glyph.

Copy glyph A (eight bytes at $6800 + A*8) inverted (EOR $FF) to $14/$15, then advance $14/$15 by eight to the next character cell. The status line's cells are hires, so the inversion draws the screen byte's background colour as the letters.
Set the glyph destination $14/$15 to $4000 + A*8: cell A of the first bitmap row, the status line.

Map object X's path position $62/$63+X (0 to $222) to ramp coordinates: s < $111 indexes the (x, y) pairs of ramp_profile ($2FA1) directly (left half), s >= $111 as $222 - s (right half, mirrored), and the half is rotated into bit 7 of $57+X. Stores x in $55+X and y in $56+X, and leaves $12/$13 just past the pair.
Zero $12-$7F, the event's zero-page variables. Called from ramp_init.
Build the quarter-square tables for multiply_8x8: floor(n*n/4) for n = 0-511, low bytes at $0400-$05FF, high bytes at $0600-$07FF. Called from ramp_init.

Fill reverse_bits_table at $3363 (each byte with its eight bits reversed) and reverse_pixel_pairs_table at $3463 (its four two-bit pixels reversed), used to mirror hires and multicolour sprite rows. Called from ramp_init.

Unsigned 8 x 8 multiply: returns A*Y with the low byte in A and the high byte in Y, as q(A+Y) - q(|A-Y|) with q from the tables at $0400-$07FF. Writes A into the operands at $16E7/$16EE so that the indexed loads read q(A+Y). Uses X. The same code as High Jump's $136A.
Low byte of the operand of LDA $0481,Y, rewritten with the multiplicand by $16D3 so that the load reads q(A+Y) (the table base $0400 plus A plus Y, the $81 here being the leftover of the last call).
Low byte of the operand of LDA $0681,Y, rewritten with the multiplicand by $16D6, for the high byte of q(A+Y).

Build one 64-byte sprite block mirrored left to right for hires data: read the descriptor ($1782), clear the bytes after its last index $18, then for each three-byte row swap the outer bytes and reverse the bits of all three (reverse_bits_table); advance to the next descriptor and block ($179A).
Like mirror_hires_sprite_block, but reverses the two-bit pixels of each byte (reverse_pixel_pairs_table at $3463), mirroring multicolour sprite data.
Build one 64-byte sprite block unmirrored: clear the bytes after the descriptor's last index $18 and copy bytes $18 down to 0 from the source, then advance ($179A).

Read the six-byte sprite descriptor at ($2A): bytes 0-1 plus the base at $3351/$3352 ($8084) give the source in $12/$13, byte 2 the index of its last byte in $18. Bytes 3 and 4 are the X and Y offsets that $0C70 adds.
Advance the descriptor pointer $2A/$2B by six and the output pointer $14/$15 by 64, to the next sprite block.
Move the skater one unit back across the ramp: decrease the depth $5F/$60 by one unless it is below $00C0. Called for the stick pushed up ($1C07, $1C1A).
Move the skater one unit forward across the ramp: increase the depth $5F/$60 by one while it is below $0100. Called for the stick pulled down ($1C10, $1C45).

Physics step for object X: look up its pair ($162C). Unless the pair is one of the last 17 (index 257 or more: $12/$13, left just past the pair, is $31A5 or more, and then the velocity is not changed), the acceleration $18 is the y of the pair 17 places on minus the y of the next pair (the slope); the velocity $5B/$5C+X gains it on the left half and loses it on the right. The 24-bit path position $61-$63+X then gains the sign-extended velocity. A position below 0 is clamped to 0 and one past $222 to $0222 (fraction $FF), and each clamp increments the border colour $D020: a debugging aid left in, which flashes the border when a skater runs off either end of the path.
Ballistic step for object 1, the body thrown in a fall of type 0 or 1: add 1 to x $64, add the vertical velocity $6A/$6B to $4D/$65 (fraction, y), then add $10 to the velocity (gravity).

Swap the sprite buffers ($22 flips between $A8 and $B0, so $6A00 or $6C00) and build five sprite blocks from pose $5D's 30-byte record (set_pose_pointer): copies when $57 bit 7 is set (right half), mirrored (hires blocks 1, 4, 5; multicolour 2 and 3) when clear. During a fall ($25 negative) blocks 1-4 come from the thrown body's pose $6C (side $66) and block 5, the board, from pose $5D's fifth descriptor. Mirrored, the thrown body's blocks go hires, hires, multicolour, multicolour ($18B2-$18BB), while sprite 1 is multicolour and sprite 3 hires ($D01C = 6): blocks 2 and 4 are mirrored with the wrong table (the same order as High Jump's $152B).

Draw the trick score $2C/$2D (BCD) into the score sprites as four digits, from the font's digit glyphs at $6980 (glyph $30 + digit): the thousands digit into sprite $AD ($6B40) byte column 1 and the hundreds into column 2, the tens and units into sprite $AE ($6B80) columns 0 and 1, each eight rows from row 2 ($1920). The thousands digit is blank when zero, the hundreds digit blank when the whole high byte is zero; the last two are always drawn. Called by the band-0 interrupt when the points are awarded.
Copy the eight bytes of the font glyph at $6900 + A into the score sprites at $6B40 + Y, one byte every third address (one sprite row each).
Pseudo-random byte: a shift-and-subtract step on $30 with $31 rotated in, returning ($30 + $31) EOR the frame counter $32.
Return a random number from 0 to A - 1: the high byte of random_byte * A (multiply_8x8).
Increment the 16-bit frame counter $32/$33. Called once a frame from the band-0 interrupt; $32 also feeds random_byte and the crowd timers' every-fourth-frame step.

Enter phase A ($34) and clear the animation counters $37/$38 (at $1AAB), with each phase's entry work: 0 depth $C8, trick score and channel record cleared, SCORE and PASSES redrawn; 2 (a new pass) is a fall of type 2 at once if over the channel, otherwise the start speed of the side ($1E3B), pumps, spin, grab, lean and drift state cleared, the trick score doubled if the skater left the left wall and has come back over the other side of the channel ($49), the pop-up timer $2E = 60 if there are points to award, and the pass count $4C raised; 4 the spin rate $3C = $59, or $47 for class 1; 6 a trick score of 200; $12 500; $16 300, with $39 = $FF if left or right is held; $18 250; $10 the trick score doubled and sound 23 ended ($3719 = 1); 8 sound 23 ended; $0A the thrown body (object 1) set up from the skater (position, side, depth, a sideways slide $6D = $7A or $86, for type 2 the start speed) and the fall sound fall_sounds[$28]; $1E the skater put at the wall top and the variety bonus counted ($1E48). Phase 2's check of the width ($1D26) only sets $28 = 1, which the clearing straight after undoes.
Left held in the air: if the spin mode $39 is the right-press one (bits 7 and 5 set) check for a stop ($1AF9); otherwise set $39 = $C0 (spinning, left mode), so holding left keeps the spin going.
Right held in the air: if $39 is in the left-press mode (bit 7 set, bit 5 clear) check for a stop ($1AF9); otherwise set $39 = $E0 (spinning, right mode).
Up held in the air: if the drift mode $3A is the down one (bits 7 and 5 set) stop the drift ($1AF2); otherwise $3A = $C0 (drifting back).
Down held in the air: if $3A is in the up mode (bit 7 set, bit 5 clear) stop the drift ($1AF2); otherwise $3A = $E0 (drifting forward).
Clear bit 6 of the drift mode $3A ($3A AND $A0): the drift stops, the mode bits stay.

The opposite direction pressed during a spin: stop it (clear bit 6 of $39) in trick class 1 at once, otherwise only when the step count $29 is exactly 8 (half a turn) or 16 or more. Pressing against the spin therefore stops it on a half or whole turn, which the landing needs.
Air controls, the spin: left held ($1AB2), right held ($1AC2); then while $39 bit 6 is set, one spin step in the mode's direction (spin_step_left $154E, or spin_step_right $1578 when bit 5 is set).

Air and plant controls, across the ramp: up held ($1AD2), down held ($1AE2); in phase 6 a press while $27 is nonzero also requests sound 23 and clears $27, so the sound starts once. Then while $3A bit 6 is set the depth drifts by -$7F/256 a frame (up mode, $81) or +$7F/256 (down mode).
Friction on the skater (X = 0): move the speed $5B/$5C one unit towards zero.
Friction for object X ($1B81 with X = $0F is object 1): add 1 to a negative speed, subtract 1 from a positive one, leave zero alone.
Four calls of friction on object 1 (through $1BA6, $1BA9, $1BAC): the sliding body in a type-2 fall slows by four units a frame.
Two calls of friction on object 1 (entry inside friction_object1_x4).
One call of friction on object 1 through $1BAC, then return through it (entry inside friction_object1_x4).
JMP to apply_friction_x with X = $0F (object 1).

Fire held while riding (phase 2): only the first such frame in each half of the ramp counts ($26, cleared at the centre crossing): if the skater is then in the pump band, y $E0-$EF, count a pump in $3F and add $50 to the speed in the direction of travel. A press anywhere else uses up the half's pump.

Swoosh sounds while riding: from the start of a pass ($27 = 0, set_phase) sound 15 when the skater goes down into the lower ramp ($23 >= $E0); after the centre crossing ($27 = 1, band-1 interrupt) sound 16 when it climbs out ($23 < $F0); each time $27 then becomes $FF, so each plays once per half.
Riding: stick up moves the skater back across the ramp (depth_step_back), down moves it forward (depth_step_forward).

On the platform: up steps the depth back, but not into the channel (then $D8) or below $C3; down steps it forward, out of the channel to $E8. The skater can stand on either side of the channel but not in it.

In the lower zones of phase 2: a newly pressed left or right sets the lean flags: against the direction of travel (the sign of the speed $5C) gives $40 = $FF, $41 = 0; with it gives $40 = 0, $41 = $FF.

Choose the trick class $42 for the coming wall: class 6 (end of the run) once the pass count $4C is 11 or more; otherwise by the pumps $3F (0-2): no lean, class 0 (class_by_pumps_none); a lean against the travel ($40), 5, 4 or 3 (class_by_pumps_back); a lean with it ($41), 2, 2 or 1 (class_by_pumps_with).
Draw the total score $43-$45 (BCD) as five digits at status-line cells $22-$26 with leading-zero blanking ($46), the units always drawn. The sixth digit (the high nibble of $45) is never shown.
Draw the pass count $4C at cells $18-$19: a 1 and a 0 for 10 or more (so 11 also shows as 10), otherwise a blank and the digit.
Add the signed fraction A to the depth $5E/$5F/$60 (A >= $80 counts as A - 256). Used for every drift across the ramp.
Carry set when the skater is over the channel: on the left half of the ramp only, with the depth $5F/$60 from $D9 to $E6.
Carry set when the depth is outside the ramp's width, below $BF or $101 and above.
Double the trick score $2C/$2D (decimal mode).
Add the trick score $2C/$2D to the total $43-$45 (decimal mode, carry into the top byte) and redraw it (draw_total_score).
Add A to the pose pointer $2A/$2B ($18 skips four six-byte parts to the fifth, the board; 6 skips one).
Keep the depth $5F/$60 within $00A8-$0108. Called every frame from the band-1 interrupt.
During a fall: add the signed slide $6D to the depth fraction and move $6D two units towards zero, so the fallen skater slides across the ramp and stops.

A fall off the side of the ramp (the depth outside its width): on the back half (depth below $E0) while $4E lasts, $4F gains $4E and each carry moves x $55 one right and the depth one back, $4E losing 4 each frame; pose 0. The skater drops: below y $F0 the speed gains $10 a frame and y $56 gains the speed; at $F0 it bounces, the speed halved and reversed (a downward speed is zeroed first). Then double friction and the display position.
Compare the depth with $E0: carry set when $5F/$60 >= $00E0 (the far side of the channel's middle).
Return X/Y = the speed a new pass starts with: $0280 on the left half, $FD80 (-$0280) on the right.

Variety bonus at the end of the run: count the bits set in $50, one per kind of trick landed (bit 0 air, 1 class-1 air, 2 class 2, 3 class 3, 4 class 4, 5 class 5), and put variety_bonus[n] (0, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 6000, 9000) in the trick score, with the pop-up timer if it is not zero.

Flip two-frame animated cell A (0-$44) of the picture: bitmap address $4000 + the word cell_bitmap_offsets[A] ($1FF8); bit 7 of cell_colours[2A] ($210C) toggles to pick frame 2A or 2A+1; that frame's screen byte ($2082) goes to $6400 + offset/8, its colour ($210C) to $D800 + offset/8, and its eight bitmap bytes from cell_pixels ($2196) + frame*8. The same code and cell data as High Jump's $192E.
Animate cells A and A+1 with animate_cell (a flag is two cells).

From the band-0 interrupt: when a random byte AND 7 is zero, animate a random flag (cells 0-7, as pairs A = 0, 2, 4 or 6) and return carry set; otherwise carry clear, and the caller tries two crowd cells.

If a random byte is not above $52, animate one random cell from 8 to $44 (the crowd). $52 is loaded when points are awarded (band-0 interrupt, $0B60: half of $30 + twice the trick score's high byte) and counted down every fourth frame once $53 has run out, so the crowd moves more and for longer after bigger tricks. Called twice a frame by the band-0 interrupt and up to ten times by band 1.

Event state at each entry: queue the music (sound 1) unless sound is off ($FE10), clear the total score $43-$45, the pass count $4C and the variety bits $50, copy one of the two sprite colour sets ($3313 or $331B, picked at random) into $D027-$D02E, and enter phase 0.

Every frame from band 1: show sprite 7 (the board's black shadow, $73 = $80, ORed into $D015) while the depth is within the ramp's width, else $73 = 0; then update its reference point (shadow_position $1517).
Add A (BCD) to the trick score $2C/$2D (decimal mode). The held tricks call it every frame: 2 or 4 in the class-2 plant, 5 in class 3, 2 in a grab.

Every frame from the band-0 interrupt: compare keyboard row 7 ($DC01, with $DC00 = $7F) with the previous value $7A; a newly pressed RUN/STOP (bit 7) sets $FE12 = $FF and ends the event through end_event, from inside the interrupt.

Every frame from the band-0 interrupt: a newly pressed C= key (row 7 bit 5, previous value $7B) flips the sound-off flag $FE10 and copies it to $7C (the main loop then resets the driver); turning sound back on queues sound 1.

End of the event (after phase $1E with fire, or RUN/STOP): hand the total score to the event manager as three BCD bytes, $43 (tens and units) in $FE03, $44 in $FE04, $45 in $FE05; turn all sprites off ($D015 = 0), reset the sound driver ($271E) and JMP $FE06. Reached from inside the interrupt, which never returns (no RTI).
Append sound ID A to the 16-entry ring $3353 at write index $7D, with no overflow check. The main loop drains it ($1FC2, $275C).
Return the next sound ID from the ring $3353 and advance the read index $7E; the main loop calls it while $7E differs from $7D.

Unpack run-length data from ($12) to ($14) until $12/$13 reaches the end address in $16/$17: a control byte $00-$7F copies the next n+1 bytes; $80-$FF repeats the next byte n-$7F times. Called once, from load_ramp_picture.

Animated-cell table read by animate_cell ($1E68): one little-endian word per cell number 0-$44, the cell offset into the bitmap (bitmap at $4000 + word; screen and colour bytes at word/8). Entry 0 is $0408. The 69 words run $1FF8-$2081. The same table as High Jump's $1B91.

High byte of cell_bitmap_offsets entry 0; animate_cell reads the high bytes as $1FF9,X and the low bytes as $1FF8,X with X = 2 x cell. Entries 0-7 are the flag cells animate_flag_pair flips, 8-$44 the crowd cells animate_crowd_cell flips.
cell_bitmap_offsets from entry 32 (cell $20, offset $0A70) on; still the table read by animate_cell.
cell_bitmap_offsets entry 55 (offset $0BD8, the crowd cell at text row 9, column 19).

Entries 56-68 of the animated-cell offset table from $1FF8: bitmap offsets ($0BE0-$0D50) of the last crowd cells, rows 9-10. $1E68 derives the bitmap address ($4000+offset), the screen byte ($6400+offset/8) and the colour-RAM byte from each.

Screen-matrix byte (multicolour bitmap colours %01 high nibble, %10 low nibble) for each animated cell and frame, two bytes per cell (frame 0, frame 1): this label covers cells 0-31. $1E68 writes the chosen frame's byte to $6400 + cell offset/8. Cells 0-7 are the four flags of text row 3, cells 8-68 the crowd in rows 7-10.
Screen-matrix colour bytes, frame 0 then frame 1, for animated cells 32-63 (crowd, text rows 8-9); continues anim_cell_screen_colours.
Screen-matrix colour bytes for the last animated cells 64-68 (crowd, rows 9-10), frame 0 then frame 1; ends at $210B.

Colour-RAM byte (colour of %11 pixels, low nibble) per animated cell and frame, two bytes per cell, cells 0-31 here. Bit 7 of each cell's first byte is the frame flag: $1E68 flips it at $1E94 and shows frame 1 when it ends up set, so the table is rewritten during play.
Colour-RAM bytes and frame flags (bit 7 of the first byte) for animated cells 32-63; continues anim_cell_colour_ram.
Colour-RAM bytes and frame flags for animated cells 64-68; ends at $2195.

Bitmap pixels of the animated background cells, 8 bytes per frame, frame 0 then frame 1 of each cell (entry = cell*2 + frame), copied to the bitmap at $4000 + cell offset by $1EC0-$1EC7. This label: cells 0-3 (the two left flags on row 3).
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 4-7 (flags), at $21D6-$2215.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 8-11 (crowd), at $2216-$2255.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 12-15 (crowd), at $2256-$2295.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 16-19 (crowd), at $2296-$22D5.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 20-23 (crowd), at $22D6-$2315.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 24-27 (crowd), at $2316-$2355.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 28-31 (crowd), at $2356-$2395.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 32-35 (crowd), at $2396-$23D5.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 36-39 (crowd), at $23D6-$2415.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 40-43 (crowd), at $2416-$2455.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 44-47 (crowd), at $2456-$2495.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 48-51 (crowd), at $2496-$24D5.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 52-55 (crowd), at $24D6-$2515.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 56-59 (crowd), at $2516-$2555.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 60-63 (crowd), at $2556-$2595.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 64-67 (crowd), at $2596-$25D5.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cell 68 (crowd), at $25D6-$25E5.

156 bytes loaded with file $0D that no instruction reads (code scan) and that the simulated runs neither read nor write: irregular values, apparently stale memory saved with the file. High Jump has a gap of the same size at the same place in its layout ($217F-$221A, between the cell bitmaps and the sound driver's state), with other bytes in it.

Number of sound IDs waiting in pending_sound_ids ($26DE), 0-16. queue_sound_id ($275C) appends while it is below $10 (a 17th request is dropped); update_sid_voices ($2793) drains it to zero each tick. Cleared with the rest of $2682-$26ED by init_sound_driver.

Lowest priority among the three slots (the one a new sound must equal or beat). Recomputed at $2E23-$2E3C after each start; set to 0 when a slot finishes ($2D88), so the next request always wins that free slot.
Slot offset (0, 2 or 4) of the slot holding sound_weakest_priority: where start_sound_on_weakest_slot ($2DE8) puts the next accepted sound. Set at $2E3F and, when a slot ends, at $2D8B.
The primary-script command byte being executed, saved by dispatch_sound_opcode ($27FD). Handlers test its bit 7 (BIT $2685) for the operand mode and op 7 re-reads its high nibble.
Low byte of the left-hand value for sound op 6 (compare): the slot's frequency, pulse width, sustain level, loop counter or a byte read from memory; $2687 holds the high byte for 16-bit compares.
High byte of the 16-bit left-hand compare value (frequency or pulse width) for sound op 6, compared first at $2B14.
Low byte (or only byte) of the right-hand operand of sound op 6, fetched by $2B30/$2B43 from the script or through an address.
High byte of the right-hand operand for 16-bit compares in sound op 6 (set by $2B43).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency low byte, at $268A/$268C/$268E for slot offsets 0/2/4 (voices 3/2/1). Written with every frequency change and read back by op 4 (add) and op 6 (compare).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency high byte, at $268B/$268D/$268F for slot offsets 0/2/4; paired with slot_freq_lo.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width low byte, at $2690/$2692/$2694 for slot offsets 0/2/4; set by op 1 and note command $AD, added to by op 4, compared by op 6.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width high nibble, at $2691/$2693/$2695 for slot offsets 0/2/4.

Low byte of slot 0's call-stack base address (init_sound_driver stores $EE, so slot 0 nests at $26EE); the three slots' base pointers are words at $2696, $2698, $269A, read as $2696,x at $2A6F and $2D8F.
High byte of slot 0's call-stack base ($26), read as $2697,x with the low byte at $2696,x.
Low byte of slot 2's (SID voice 2's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $FE, so slot 2 nests at $26FE.
High byte of slot 2's call-stack base ($26).
Low byte of slot 4's (SID voice 1's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $0E, so slot 4 nests at $270E.
High byte of slot 4's call-stack base ($27).

Four note durations per slot, $269C-$269F (slot 0), $26A0-$26A3 (slot 2), $26A4-$26A7 (slot 4), indexed by slot*2 + bits 7-6 of a note byte. The chosen value goes to the slot's wait timer ($26B4,x). Loaded by op $97 and note command $5D.

Four gate lengths per slot, $26A8-$26AB, $26AC-$26AF, $26B0-$26B3, chosen like slot_note_durations. Non-zero: the note sets the gate bit and the gate timer ($26B5,x); zero: the note changes pitch without re-gating. Loaded by op $A7 and note command $6D.

Per-slot wait timer at $26B4/$26B6/$26B8 (slot offsets 0/2/4): while non-zero update_sid_voices decrements it instead of reading the script; a value N set in one tick makes the slot read again N+1 ticks later (checked against SID writes in the simulator). Set by op 8, notes and note commands.

Per-slot gate timer at $26B5/$26B7/$26B9: when flag bit 5 is set it counts down each tick and, G+1 ticks after a value G was set, clears the gate bit (bit 0) of the voice's control register ($27C4), starting the release. The shadow $26C1,x keeps the gate bit.
Sound ID playing in each slot, at $26BA/$26BC/$26BE; 0 after the slot ends. stop_sound ($276A) searches it.
Per-slot flags at $26BB/$26BD/$26BF: 0 idle; bit 6 active (set to $40 at start); bit 5 gate timer running; bit 4 inside a script call (call stack non-empty); bit 7 paused (skipped by the updater).
Per-slot sustain level counter (low nibble used) at $26C0/$26C2/$26C4: op $24 adds to it and writes it as the high nibble of the SID sustain/release register; op $26 compares it.
Per-slot shadow of the SID control register (waveform bits and gate) at $26C1/$26C3/$26C5; the gate timer clears bit 0 from it, notes set bit 0.
Per-slot loop counter at $26C6/$26C8/$26CA: set by op $31, added to by op $34, compared by op $36, and decremented by the loop op $15 (jump while non-zero).

Priority of the sound in slot 0 (SID voice 3); the slots' priorities are at $26C7/$26C9/$26CB. Set from sound_priorities ($3597) on start, cleared at end; compared at $2E23-$2E3C to find the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 2 (SID voice 2), read directly at $2E28/$2E2F when finding the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 4 (SID voice 1), read directly at $2E25 when finding the weakest slot (slot 4 is the first candidate).
Per-slot shadow of the SID attack/decay register at $26CC/$26CE/$26D0; set by op $41 and note command $8D.
Per-slot shadow of the SID sustain/release register at $26CD/$26CF/$26D1; op $24 rewrites its high nibble from slot_sustain_level.

Bytes used on each slot's call stack at $26D2/$26D4/$26D6 (two per nested call); a call pushes the return pointer at stack base + depth, a return pops it. Not range-checked: more than 8 nested calls would run into the next slot's stack.
Result of the slot's last op 6 compare at $26D3/$26D5/$26D7, as the processor's C and Z bits: 0 less, 1 greater, 3 equal. Tested by the conditional jumps of op 5 against $2A9C/$2AA2.

Per-slot octave shift at $26D8/$26DA/$26DC: the number of right shifts applied to note frequencies before the note's own octave bits are added (note_frequency, $2D4A). Set by op $B7 and note command $4D.
Sixteen-byte queue of requested sound IDs: queue_sound_id ($275C) appends while sound_pending_count is below $10; update_sid_voices starts them newest first and empties the queue each tick.

Three 16-byte call stacks for nested sound scripts, $26EE (slot 0), $26FE (slot 2), $270E (slot 4), addressed through slot_stack_ptr_lo/hi. Each call pushes a two-byte return address. Not cleared by init: the bytes here are whatever the file carried; 8 levels per slot.

Sound driver reset: zero the script pointers $02-$07 and all driver state $2682-$26ED, silence the three SID control registers, set volume $0F with no filter ($D418), and point the slots' call stacks at $26EE/$26FE/$270E. Called at $08C8, from the main loop when $7C is set ($08D3), and at $1FAD.

Request sound ID A: append it to pending_sound_ids unless 16 are already waiting (then the request is silently dropped). Called from the main loop ($08E3, IDs from the game's own request ring at $1FC2) and by sound op 2. Clobbers X.

Stop sound ID A wherever it plays: search slot_sound_id for slots 4, 2, 0 and, if found, silence that slot through $2D77 with interrupts disabled. No caller in the Freestyle program (instruction and byte-pair scan); part of the shared driver.

records.s: Found: Y = the slot's SID register offset; silence the slot with IRQs masked.

records.c: Set slot A (0-2, doubled to the slot offset) to flags $80 so update_sid_voices skips it. It replaces all flags rather than setting bit 7. No caller in this program (instruction and byte-pair scan).
Clear bit 7 of slot A's flags. After pause_sound_slot the flags are $80, so this leaves 0 (idle) and the slot does not resume. No caller in this program.

One sound tick (run by the main loop once per raster frame counted in $7F): start every queued ID (start_sound_on_weakest_slot), then for slots 4, 2, 0 (SID voices 1, 2, 3): skip if idle or paused; run the gate timer; if the wait timer is zero, execute script commands until a $00 byte (end of tick) or the slot ends.
Read the next byte of slot X's primary script through ($02,X) and advance the pointer; the Z flag reflects the byte (a $00 byte ends the tick at $27E1).

Execute primary command A: save it in sound_command_byte, push the handler for its low nibble from $2815/$2825 (RTS trick), and enter it with A = high nibble. Bit 7 of the command is the operand-mode flag; bits 6-4 select the sub-operation.

High bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one, indexed by the low nibble of the command: 0 end/return ($2D70), 1 set register ($2835), 2 queue sound ($28F9), 3 poke/wait ($2908), 4 add ($2973), 5 jump/loop/call ($2A02), 6 compare ($2AA8), 7 note stream ($2B61), 8 wait ($2D58), 9 end, A call 6502 code ($2DB8), B-F end.
Low bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one (paired with $2815); RTS lands one byte higher, on the handler.

Op $x1, set a voice register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency (2 bytes lo,hi), 1-2 pulse width (2), 3 loop counter (1), 4 attack/decay (1), 5 sustain/release (1), 6-7 control/waveform (1). Bit 7 clear: the value follows in the script; bit 7 set: a 2-byte address follows and the value is read from there. Writes the SID and the slot shadow.
Op $02: the next script byte is a sound ID to request through queue_sound_id (started at the next tick, by priority); X and Y preserved.

Op 3 with an address operand (2 bytes). Sub-op 1 ($13/$93), wait-until: compare memory at the address with a value (bit 7 set: a literal byte; clear: a byte read through a second address); if unequal, back the script up 4 bytes and end this slot's tick, so it retries next tick. Other sub-ops ($03/$83), poke: store a value there (bit 7 clear: literal; set: read through a second address).

records.s: Unequal: rewind the script by 4 (right for the literal form $93 aa aa vv; the address form is 5 bytes long, so it would resume on its second byte), drop the dispatcher's return and go to the next slot.

records.c: Op 4, add to a register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency += 2-byte value (bit 7 set: value read through an address), 1 pulse width += 2 bytes, 2 sustain level += byte, rewrite sustain/release and set the gate bit (re-trigger), 3+ loop counter += byte. Writes the SID and the shadows; 16-bit adds wrap.

Op 5, script flow. Bit 7 clear: $05 jump to a 2-byte address; $15 decrement the loop counter, jump while non-zero, else skip the address; $25 call (push the return pointer on the slot's stack, set flag bit 4); $35 replace this slot's sound with the ID in the next byte; others end. Bit 7 set: conditional jump on the last compare, $85 equal, $95 less, $A5 not equal, $B5 greater, $C5 less or equal, $D5 greater or equal; $E5/$F5 end.
First accepted compare result for the conditional jumps $85-$D5 (index = bits 6-4): 3,0,1,1,0,1. A jump is taken when slot_compare_result equals this byte or the one at $2AA2.
Second accepted compare result for the conditional jumps (same index): 3,0,0,1,3,3. With $2A9C this gives equal, less, not equal (1 or 0), greater, less-or-equal (0 or 3), greater-or-equal (1 or 3).

Op 6, compare and keep the result in slot_compare_result, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency vs 2-byte operand, 1 pulse width vs 2 bytes, 2 sustain level vs byte, 3 loop counter vs byte, 7 the byte at a 2-byte address vs byte; others end the script. Bit 7 set: the operand is read through an address instead.

records.s: Bytes 2C A9 01: BIT $01A9 hides LDA #$01 at $2B2A, the entry for 'greater' (result 1); entered at $2B29 it gives 0, 'less'.

records.c: Fetch op 6's one-byte right operand into sound_compare_right: the next script byte, or (command bit 7 set) the byte read through a 2-byte address.
Fetch op 6's two-byte right operand into sound_compare_right/_hi: two script bytes, or (command bit 7 set) the word read through a 2-byte address.

Op 7. Bit 7 clear ($07): play the next event of the slot's note stream at ($08,X): low nibble 0-C a note (frequency table index, 0 silent), bits 5-4 extra octave shift, bits 7-6 pick duration and gate length; $xD a note command (handler $2C54 by high nibble, next byte its argument); $0E call a primary-script subroutine at the next 2 bytes; else end. Bit 7 set: $87 set the stream pointer, $97 four durations, $A7 four gate lengths, $B7 octave shift.
Read the next byte of slot X's note stream through ($08,X) and advance that pointer.

Low bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, indexed by the high nibble of a $xD stream byte: 0 note+duration, 1 frequency+duration, 2 note+duration+gate, 3 frequency+duration+gate, 4 octave shift, 5 durations, 6 gate lengths, 7 control, 8 attack/decay, 9 sustain/release, A pulse width. $BD-$FD index past the table (no check).
High bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, paired with note_command_handlers_lo; read at $2BBE and jumped to through $0E/$0F.
Note command $0D: the argument is a note byte (low nibble note, bits 5-4 octave); the next stream byte is a literal duration for the wait timer. Sets the frequency without touching the gate.
Note command $1D: the argument and the next byte are a literal SID frequency (low, high); the next byte is the duration. No gate change.
Note command $2D: note byte argument, then a literal duration and gate length; starts the gate timer (flag bit 5) but does not set the gate bit itself.
Note command $3D: literal frequency (argument = low, next = high), then duration and gate length; starts the gate timer without setting the gate bit.
Note command $4D: the argument becomes the slot's octave shift ($26D8,x); then the next stream event is played in the same tick.
Note command $5D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four note durations ($269C); then the next event is played.
Note command $6D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four gate lengths ($26A8); then the next event is played.
Note command $7D: write the argument to the voice's SID control register (waveform, gate) and its shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $8D: write the argument to the voice's attack/decay register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $9D: write the argument to the voice's sustain/release register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $AD: the argument and the next stream byte are the pulse width (low, high), written to the SID and shadows; then the next event is played.

Note number A (0-15) to frequency in $0E/$0F: read the top-octave value from note_freq_lo/hi and shift it right by (bits 5-4 of the note byte in $11) + the slot's octave shift. Used by notes and note commands $0D/$2D.

Op 8: the next byte is a wait. $08 N: set the slot's wait timer, so the script resumes N+1 ticks later (once a $00 has ended this tick). $88 G: set the gate timer instead and flag bit 5, so the gate is released G+1 ticks later while the script runs on.
Op 0/9/B-F (and every invalid sub-op): if the slot is inside a call (flag bit 4), pop the return pointer from its call stack and continue there; otherwise fall into silence_sound_slot.

End slot X: clear the voice's control register (gate off, no waveform), the slot's ID, flags, stack depth and priority, and make it the weakest slot (priority 0) for the next request. Y = the voice's SID register offset. Also called from stop_sound.

Op $0A: call the 6502 routine at the 2-byte address that follows, preserving X and Y. The music's two voice scripts (file $13) use it to call $E0A7 and $E0C0, which pick the next phrase; sound 18 calls $3807 and $381C.
JMP ($000E): the indirect call made by sound_opA_call_code; returns to $2DC9 when the called routine executes RTS.

Read a 2-byte address from slot X's script and return the byte there in A and the following byte in $11 (a little-endian word), with Y restored to the voice's SID register offset. The operand form used when a command's bit 7 selects it.

Start sound ID A if its priority (sound_priorities, $3597) is at least sound_weakest_priority: replace the sound in slot sound_weakest_slot. Equal priority wins, so a new sound replaces an old one of the same rank.

Start sound ID Y with priority A on slot X: set the slot's priority and ID, its script pointer from sound_script_addresses ($3563/$357D), clear its timers and stack, set flags $40, zero the voice's seven SID registers, then find the new weakest slot (slot 4 first, then 2, then 0) for sound_weakest_priority/slot. Also used by op $35.

SID register offset of each sound slot, read at even X only: $2E43 (slot 0) $0E = voice 3, $2E45 (slot 2) $07 = voice 2, $2E47 (slot 4) $00 = voice 1. The odd bytes $2E44/$2E46 are never read as offsets.

Low bytes of the note frequency table, 16 entries indexed by the note's low nibble: 0 silence ($0000), 1-12 the twelve semitones A, A#, B, C ... G# of the top octave ($70C7 ... $D4E6), 13-15 zero. In NTSC SID units entry 1 is 1760 Hz (A6); on a PAL machine it plays about 0.65 semitone flat.

High bytes of the note frequency table ($00,$70,$77,$7E,$86,$8E,$96,$9F,$A8,$B3,$BD,$C8,$D4,0,0,0); each step is a factor of about 1.0595, one semitone. note_frequency shifts the value right once per octave down.
Raster band handler addresses, one word per band, read by raster_irq into its JSR at $0B0F: band 0 $0B25 (irq_band0_bottom), band 1 $0CCE (irq_band1_play).
High bytes of irq_band_handlers (read as $2E69,X with X = 2 * band).
Raster compare line of each band: $FB for band 0 (below the picture), $38 for band 1 (just above it).
Next band after each band: 1 after band 0, 0 after band 1.
Riding pose in the top zone of the wall for each trick class $42 (0-6): $08, $18, $30, $47, $08, $18, $08. Read by phase 2 at $0E53 (class_ride_poses_fakie instead while the fakie flag $24 is set).
The same for a fakie skater ($24 set): $10, $20, $35, $4E, $10, $20, $10.
The phase each trick class starts on reaching the coping ($0E7C): class 0 and 1 phase 4 (air), 2 phase 6, 3 phase $12, 4 phase $16, 5 phase $18, 6 phase $1C (the end of the run).
Per trick class, nonzero when the skater's displayed y is held at the coping instead of rising above it (move_skater $14A2): 0 for the air classes 0 and 1, 1 for classes 2-6.
Trick class for 0, 1, 2 pumps with no lean: 0, 0, 0 (choose_trick_class $1CA2).
Trick class for 0, 1, 2 pumps with a lean against the direction of travel ($40): 5, 4, 3.
Trick class for 0, 1, 2 pumps with a lean in the direction of travel ($41): 2, 2, 1.

Riding poses by height, five triples (threshold, pose, fakie pose) searched for the first threshold above the skater's y $23 ($0E25, and $0EA4 with the pose at $2E96 in a fall): below $BA $FF (take the class pose), below $D6 $03/$07, below $E3 $02/$06, below $EC $01/$05, otherwise $00/$04.
Second byte of ride_pose_zones' first triple; the fall phase reads the triples' pose bytes from here ($0EA9).
The same triples used while fire is held (pumping): identical except the lowest zone, $28/$29, a crouch.
Class-2 plant poses $30-$34, stepped through by phase 6 (and backwards by phase 8); the fifth is held.
The class-2 plant poses for a fakie skater: $35-$39.

Eight poses of phase $10 (leaving the plant with a turn), four tables of eight by the fakie flag $24 and the direction flag $39: $2EBD (neither), $2EC5 ($39), $2ECD ($24), $2ED5 (both). Each runs back through the plant poses and on into the spin poses $18-$26.
plant_turn_poses for $39 set, $24 clear: $34 $33 $32 $31 $18 $26 $24 $22.
plant_turn_poses for $24 and $39 set: $39 $38 $37 $36 $20 $1E $1C $1A.
Ten poses of the push-off from the platform, one per six frames (phase 0): $81, $86, $40-$46, $30. Entry 0 is also the pose built at start-up ($09FB).

Two-pose pairs for the grabs, addressed by immediate pointers at $1002-$102D (no instruction names them as an operand): $2EE7 ($3A, $3A) for pose 8, $2EE9 ($3B, $3C) for pose $0C, $2EEB ($3D, $3D) for pose $10, $2EED ($3E, $3F) for pose $14. Phases $0C/$0E read them through ($1C).
Class-3 trick poses $48-$4A (phase $12 forwards, $14 backwards). The rendered shapes show the skater upside down on one hand with the board held up: a handplant, by their look.
The class-3 poses for a fakie skater: $4D, $4C, $4B.
Class-4 trick poses $53-$4F (phase $16; reversed with the fakie flag).
Class-4 poses used when left or right was held as the trick began ($39): $54-$58.
Class-5 trick poses for phase $18: $18, then $27 down to $20 (reversed with the fakie flag), half of the second 16-pose spin ring.
Pose of the thrown body in a fall of type 0 or 1 by its height $65, pairs (threshold, pose): below $A8 $2A, below $B8 $2B, below $C8 $2C, below $DC $2D, otherwise $2E.
Pose column of fall_air_poses: lda $2F09,y at $0ED2 takes the pose of the pair whose threshold ($2F08,y, compared at $0ECD) the height first falls below; $2F11 is the last pose, $2E.
Poses of the body lying after a fall of type 0, one per eight frames: $2E $2F $2E $2E.
Poses after a fall of type 1, fourteen of them: $2E, $59-$63, $62, $64 (the body rolling over).
Pose of the sliding body in a fall of type 2 by its height $65, pairs (threshold, pose): below $B0 $65, below $C8 $66, below $E0 $67, otherwise $68.
Pose column of fall_slide_poses: lda $2F25,y at $0F26 takes the pose of the first pair whose threshold ($2F24,y, compared at $0F21) the height is below; poses $65-$68.
Number of lying poses for fall types 0 and 1: 4 and 14.
Added to the body's x $64 at each lying pose: 1 for type 0, 0 for type 1.
11 bytes (00 00 00 00 01 02 02 02 02 02 02) that no instruction reads: the tables on both sides are indexed by values that never reach them.
Phase $1C (the run is over) poses: $69-$6D, then $6D held.
The same for a fakie skater, starting from $6E.
Phase $1E poses for a total score under 2,500: $6D, $6F-$74, $6D, $6D, $6D.
Phase $1E poses for a total under 10,000: $6D, $75-$7B, $7A, $6D.
Phase $1E poses for 10,000 and more: $6D, $7C-$80, $7F, $80, $80, $80 (the board raised overhead).
Fidget animation on the platform, variant 0, twelve poses: $81-$84, $84, $85, then $81 to the end.
Fidget animation, variant 1: $81, $87-$8A, $8A, $8B, then $81 to the end.
Length of each fidget variant: 12 and 12.

Phase handler addresses, one word per even phase number ($34), patched into the JMP at $0D55: 0 $0D58 platform, 2 $0E0B riding, 4 $0F50 air, 6 $103F plant, 8 $10CE plant release, $0A $0E82 fall, $0C $12D3 grab in, $0E $1307 grab hold, $10 $111C plant turn, $12 $1184 handplant hold, $14 $1213 its release, $16 $1274 class 4, $18 $1358 class 5, $1A $0DBC fidget, $1C $13B0 run over, $1E $13D9 final.
High bytes of phase_handlers (read as $2F82,X).

The half-pipe as a path: 274 (x, y) pairs, $2FA1-$31C4, indexed by the path position (0-$110 directly, $111-$222 mirrored) in lookup_path_position. Pairs 0-108 are a vertical column at x 42, y 64-172: the air above the coping (y < $96, 150) and the vertical part of the wall; the curve runs to (118, 240) at pair 209, then the flat bottom to the centre (182, 240) at pair 273. The skater stands on the platform at pair 86, (42, 150). The same table, byte for byte, as High Jump's $2ACB.
ramp_profile from pair 32 on (y 96-127, x 42).
ramp_profile from pair 64 (y 128-159, x 42); pair 86, the coping and platform height, is at $304D.
ramp_profile from pair 96: the column ends at pair 108 (y 172), then the wall curves out.
ramp_profile from pair 128 ((48, 192)).
ramp_profile from pair 160.
ramp_profile from pair 192; y reaches 240 at pair 209.
ramp_profile from pair 224, the flat bottom (y 240), to the centre at pair 273 ($31C3).
ramp_profile from pair 256: from pair 257 integrate_object_motion stops using the slope.
Sixteen glyph codes 0-9 and A-F (ASCII $30-$39, $41-$46), indexed by a digit by draw_digit ($15BF).

Sprite shape copied to block $AD ($6B40) at start-up ($0A05): the left half of a rounded box, rows 0-10, with a small plus sign in its left end. Shown as sprite 5 during the trick-score pop-up, with digits drawn into rows 2-9 ($18E3).
Sprite shape copied to block $AE ($6B80): the right half of the box, with a second plus sign; sprite 6.
X offsets of the score sprites from $A0: 0 and $18 (place_score_sprite, indexed by Y = 0 or 1).
Y offsets of the score sprites from $A0: 0 and 0. $3259-$325A (01 01) are not read.
Two bytes (01 01) between score_sprite_y and air_scores that no instruction reads.

Landing scores for the air classes other than 1, BCD words (low, high), 16 per row: the row is the number of half turns (0-4), the column the grab count $4B (score_air_landing $0FC9). Row 0 (no turn): 25, 75, 125 ... 775.
High bytes of the air_scores words (read as $325C,X).

air_scores row 1 (half a turn): 100, 175, 250, 325, 425, 500 ... 1250. The fifth entry breaks the step of 75 (325 to 425), so a half turn with four grabs is worth 425 rather than 400, and every later entry is 25 more than the step would give.
air_scores row 2 (a whole turn): 250 to 1750 in steps of 100.
air_scores row 3 (one and a half turns): 550 to 2425 in steps of 125.
air_scores row 4 (two turns): 1150 to 3400 in steps of 150. A larger index runs into the tables after it.
Landing scores for trick class 1, BCD words by half turns 0-4: 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600 (score_air_landing $0FB1).
High bytes of class1_air_scores (read as $32FC,X).
End-of-run bonus by the number of kinds of trick landed (count_variety_bonus): 0, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 6000, 9000, BCD words.
High bytes of variety_bonus (read as $3306,X).

Sprite colours $D027-$D02E, set A: 8, $0F, 7, 8, (the board, from $FE02), 1, 1, 0. Sprites 5 and 6 (the score box) white, sprite 7 (the board's shadow) black. Copied by init_event when its random pick is 0.
Entry 4 of sprite_colours_a, the board's colour, overwritten with the skater attribute $FE02 at $09F5.
Sprite colours, set B: 9, $0F, 2, 9, (board), 1, 1, 0.
Entry 4 of sprite_colours_b, overwritten with $FE02 at $09F8.

Screen-matrix bytes for the 40 cells of the hires status line (copied to $6400 at $0996): $61 (blue and white) for the name field and the numbers, $6E (blue and light blue) for the cells of 'PASSES:' (16-22) and 'SCORE:' (27-32). The glyphs are drawn inverted, so the letters show the low nibble's colour.
Sound requested at the start of a fall, by fall type $28: 22, 9, 21 ($1A89).
Three bytes (0D 0F 0E) after fall_sounds that no instruction reads.
The address of the sprite shapes, $8084, stored here by load_skater_data (the end address file $11's load returned) and added to every descriptor's offset by read_sprite_descriptor.
High byte of shape_base ($80).
Sixteen-entry ring of sound requests from the game ($1FB3 writes at $7D, $1FC2 reads at $7E). The bytes in the snapshot are stale entries.
Built at start-up by build_mirror_tables: each entry is its index with the eight bits reversed. Mirrors hires sprite rows ($16F6). The file's own bytes here are overwritten.
Built at start-up by build_mirror_tables: each entry is its index with its four two-bit pixels reversed. Mirrors multicolour sprite rows ($172E).

Twenty-six sound-script addresses in split low/high arrays, indexed by the sound ID at $2DFB/$2E00; the first points to $35B4. Sounds 1 and 2 point into file $13 ($E072 and $E095, the music); IDs 3, 24 and 25 share the empty script $35B1.
High bytes of the 26 sound-script addresses, read by $2E00 into $03,X; the low bytes are at $3563.
Twenty-six one-byte priorities indexed by sound ID; $2DE9 compares the incoming value against the current voice threshold before allocation.

Sound script for IDs 3, 24 and 25: the single byte $09, an end command, so those IDs start nothing. Sound-script bytecode, run by update_sid_voices ($2793): low nibble = command, high nibble = variant, bit 7 = operand taken from an address; $00 ends the voice's turn for this tick.
Script variable (two bytes; only $35B2 is compared): set to $FE by sounds 6, 7 and 8 when they start or finish, set to 1 by sound 0; those three loops end early when they see 1.
Sound 0: poke $35B2 = 1, yield, end. Its only effect is to stop the repeating noise of sounds 6, 7 and 8. No code in this event queues ID 0.
Sound 5: triangle wave at $6000, AD $80 SR $F9; each tick add $05C0 until $C800, gate off and subtract $0340 to $3200, up again to $E800, down to $2C00, end. Nothing in this event queues it.

Sound 6, queued at $13E9 on the first frame of phase $1E (the end of the run): set $35B2 = $FE and $3635 = 19; noise at $1000, AD $DB SR $FE; gate on for 8 ticks, off for 14, call $3637 to count $3635 down, and repeat while it is non-zero; stops early when $35B2 = 1, then SR $08, gate off, wait 18 ticks.
Repeat counter for sound 6, set to 19 by the script at $35FD and decremented by the code at $3637.
Machine code called by sound 6's script (command $0A at $361F): DEC $3635, RTS.

Sound 23: set $3719 = $FE, noise at $1000 with AD 0 SR $20, gate on, then wait a tick at a time until $3719 = 1 (sound 11 sets it). Requested at $1B4A and $1B66 (air_depth_controls) in phase 6, once per plant; the game code stops it by writing 1 to $3719 itself, at $105B and $1065 (leaving phase 6) and at $1A2B and $1AA5 (set_phase).

Sound 7: set $35B2 = $FE, noise at $2700, AD 1 SR 1, 32 repeats ($3681) of a gate-on note with release after 12 ticks and a 13-tick wait, counted down by $3683; ends early when $35B2 = 1. Nothing in this event queues it.
Repeat counter for sound 7: 32 from $365C, decremented by $3683.
Machine code called by sound 7's script at $3671: DEC $3681, RTS.
Sound 8: as sound 7 with noise at $4000, AD 0 SR 0, 40 repeats ($36B7) of release-after-9 and a 10-tick wait; ends early when $35B2 = 1. Nothing in this event queues it.
Repeat counter for sound 8: 40 from $3692, decremented by $36B9.
Machine code called by sound 8's script at $36A7: DEC $36B7, RTS.
Sound 9, the fall sound for fall type 1 (fall_sounds $334B, queued at $1A8C by set_phase): subroutines $3935 (triangle sweep), $3884 (noise sequence) and $3839, wait 34 ticks, then $3884 again.
Sound 10: three rising triangle sweeps, $1000 to $2780 by $02C0, $2400 to $3E80 by $03C0, $1800 to $5000 by $0480, then down by $0340 to $1000. Nothing in this event queues it.
Script variable for sounds 12 and 23: they set $FE and wait for 1, which sound 11 writes.
Sound 11: poke $3719 = 1, ending the hold in sounds 12 and 23. Nothing in this event queues it.

Sound 12: set $3719 = $FE; noise at $FC00 for 2 ticks, then one tick each at $1A00, $0300, $0238, $0170, $00A8 and $9C00; then noise from $0180 falling by 1 a tick for up to 43 ticks (cut short when $3719 = 1), gate off and 7 more falling ticks. Nothing in this event queues it.
Sound 13: noise from $0600 falling by $0014 a tick for 18 ticks, AD $69 SR $D8, release 12 ticks after the start (gate timer 11). Nothing in this event queues it.
Sound 14: noise from $0600 falling by $0020 a tick for 11 ticks, AD $47 SR $06, release after 7. Nothing in this event queues it.

Sound 15, queued by ramp_bottom_sounds ($1BCE) when the skater drops into the lower ramp ($23 >= $E0) after entering phase 2: noise from $0600 falling by $001A a tick for 12 ticks, AD $69 SR $08, release after 5.
Sound 16, queued by ramp_bottom_sounds ($1BD9) when the skater rises above $23 = $F0 after crossing the centre: noise from $0400 rising by $001A a tick for 12 ticks, AD $75 SR $05, release after 7.

Sound 18: call $3807 (limits $8000 and $5000), then up to 6 cycles of a triangle rising by $0900 a tick to the upper limit and falling by $0900 to the lower, calling $381C after each to lower both limits; ends early when $3831 = 1. Nothing in this event queues it.
Upper frequency limit of sound 18 (word at $3803/$3804), compared at $37E3; $3807 sets it to $8000, $381C lowers the high byte by 9 per cycle.
High byte of sound 18's upper limit, the byte $3807 and $381C change.
Lower frequency limit of sound 18 (word at $3805/$3806), compared at $37EF; set to $5000 by $3807.
High byte of sound 18's lower limit, lowered by 9 per cycle in $381C.
Machine code called by sound 18 at $37CD: store $8000 in $3803/$3804 and $5000 in $3805/$3806, preserving A.
Machine code called by sound 18 at $37FC after each cycle: subtract 9 from the high bytes $3804 and $3806.
Script variable: set to $FE by sound 18 and to 1 by sound 17; sound 18 stops when it reads 1.
Sound 17: poke $3831 = 1, yield, end; it stops sound 18. Nothing in this event queues it.

Sound 19, also called as a subroutine by sound 9: noise at $FC00 for 1 tick, noise from $00C8 rising by $012C for 3 ticks, $FC00 again, then a pulse note at $0500 (width $09C4) falling by $004B while the width grows by $0037, 8 ticks.
